name: Spinal Muscular Atrophy Associated with Central Nervous System Anomaly
aliases: Spinal Muscular Atrophy with Central Nervous System Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for SMA with CNS Anomaly

criteria.description: Progressive proximal muscle weakness with hypotonia and areflexia
Presence of central nervous system structural anomalies on MRI
Detection of pathogenic variants in SMN1 gene or related genes associated with SMA
Electromyography showing denervation and reduced motor unit potentials
Positive family history of SMA or related neuromuscular disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive proximal muscle weakness with hypotonia and areflexia, CNS anomaly on imaging, and genetic confirmation of SMN1 or related gene mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, imaging, and genetic data due to phenotypic variability.

searchTerms: gradual weakness in upper legs and arms

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hypotonia with diminished deep tendon reflexes
searchTerms: low muscle tone with weak reflexes
floppy muscles and reduced tendon reflexes
hypotonia with diminished deep tendon reflexes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Central nervous system structural anomalies detected by MRI
searchTerms: brain and spine abnormalities on MRI
structural CNS defects seen in imaging

common.symptomName: Respiratory insufficiency due to diaphragmatic weakness
Muscle atrophy predominantly in proximal limbs
searchTerms: muscle wasting in upper arms and thighs
weakness and shrinkage of main limb muscles

common.symptomName: Feeding difficulties related to bulbar muscle weakness
searchTerms: feeding problems from swallowing muscle weakness
difficulty eating due to bulbar weakness
spine curvature due to weak muscles
muscle weakness causing sideways spine bend

laboratory: Elevated creatine kinase levels may be mild or normal
Normal routine blood counts and metabolic panels
imaging: MRI showing CNS anomalies such as cortical malformations, cerebellar hypoplasia, or corpus callosum abnormalities
Muscle MRI may show fatty infiltration and atrophy
genetic: Pathogenic variants or deletions in SMN1 gene
Possible mutations in modifier genes affecting CNS development
other: Electromyography demonstrating denervation and reduced motor unit potentials
Nerve conduction studies typically normal or mildly reduced

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of CNS structural anomalies on imaging
Pure motor neuron disease without cognitive impairment
Primary muscle pathology with dystrophic changes on biopsy
Different genetic mutations involving muscle structural proteins

redFlags: Severe feeding difficulties with risk of aspiration
Early onset seizures or unexplained neurological deterioration
references: Orphanet: Spinal muscular atrophy associated with central nervous system anomaly, ORPHA:207012
